text.p: These are the leading stories in Botswana's press on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- A Botswana citizen, Adam Mabina, has been identifed in hearings of the South African Truth and Reconciliation Commission as having spied for the-then South African Defence Force (SADF) and led six cadres of the African National Congress transitting through Botswana into an SADF ambush in which they were all killed.

- The government has deferred indefinitely parts of a proposed Mass Media Communications Bill that sought to register newspapers, accredit journalists and set up a Press Council. Sections dealing with the regulation of broadcasting will go ahead to enable the establishment next year of a national television service.

- Opposition Botswana National Front MP Mokgweetsi Kgosipula has undertaken to name to the Minister of Finance and Development Planning two Motswana contractors who he alleges have stashed away seven million pula in foreign bank accounts, yet are claiming help under a government scheme to assist contractors in financial difficulties.

- Indigenous Batswana Muslims are demanding more say in the running of the Botswana Muslim Association, which they say is dominated by Muslims of Asian origin. They say the imaams (prayer leaders) and aalims (priests) all come from the ranks of the Asians; and that are denied details of the finances of the association.

- The Chief Justice of Botswana, Moleleki Mokama, died last week after a short illness. Mokama, 64, was appointed chief justice in 1992, after serving for 20 years as attorney-general. He was educated in South Africa at Tigerkloof and at Fort Hare.
- Francistown will be granted city status on August 30, when it celebrates its 100th anniversary
